llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose (local file-based rate limiter) and requests no credentials or network access; nothing in the code or SKILL.md indicates covert data exfiltration or unrelated privileges.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the delivered artifacts: a Python script plus a JSON state file that implement a local, tiered rate-limiter. No extraneous credentials, binaries, or third‑party services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrowly scoped: run the script's commands (gate, record, pause, resume, etc.) and optionally set a few RATE_LIMIT_* env vars. The SKILL.md does recommend inserting guidance into your agent's AGENTS.md / system prompt and agent loops (to 'gate' before work). That is expected for integration but is a behavioral change you should consciously accept.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no external downloads — the skill is instruction-only with included Python code, which is the lowest-risk install model. No packages or network fetches are performed by the script.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no secrets or external credentials. Optional environment variables are reasonable (provider, plan, state path, window, estimate) and align with the rate-limiter purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes a local JSON state file and a .lock file beside it; it does not request always:true, does not modify other skills, and does not alter system-wide agent configs by itself. The only persistence is the state file used to track usage.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: a local, file-backed rate limiter with no network access and no secrets required. Before installing, consider: 1) it creates and updates a JSON state file (default next to the repository); set RATE_LIMIT_STATE to a directory you control and ensure file permissions are appropriate (the script writes with 0o600). 2) The script uses fcntl-based file locking and therefore assumes a POSIX environment — it may not work on Windows without adaptation. 3) SKILL.md asks you to add gate/record calls into your agent's system prompts and cron/heartbeat logic; adding those lines changes your agent's runtime behavior — review the exact text you add and only insert it where you intend. 4) Confirm Python3 is available and that the location where the script writes state is writable but not world-readable if you run agents in multi-tenant environments. If you want an extra check, inspect scripts/rate-limiter.py line-by-line (we reviewed it; no network calls or credential access were found). If you need stricter isolation, run the script in a sandboxed environment and set RATE_LIMIT_STATE to an isolated path.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] expected: The SKILL.md explicitly instructs integrators to add rate-limiting checks into AGENTS.md / the system prompt and agent loops. This is consistent with a rate-limiter's integration model, but because it asks you to modify system prompts, you should review and accept those changes deliberately (prompt modifications can change agent behavior).
